reason: E1 and E2 support L12 precipitation and Orowan strengthening in a related alloy (Al0.7CoCrFeNi), but neither addresses AlCoCrFeNi2.1, the specific aging window, creep resistance, thermal stability, or corrosion effects; the cited evidence is therefore only loosely related to several key premises.
premises: Low-temperature annealing of AlCoCrFeNi-based eutectic alloys precipitates coherent L12 within the FCC phase
These L12 precipitates strengthen the alloy via the Orowan mechanism
The precipitation strengthening does not compromise tensile ductility
The refined microstructure resists coarsening under thermal fluctuations, indirectly enhancing corrosion resistance
The specific aging window (600–650 °C, 1–4 h) is effective for AlCoCrFeNi2.1
